prompts.prompt: These user stories for our 'Alert Rule Management' feature are approved and need to become the Kiro IDE spec requirements document so design can start. Story A: As an SRE, I want to create an alert rule with a metric, threshold and duration, so that I get paged when a service degrades. Criteria: Given I am an authenticated SRE, When I submit a valid rule, Then the rule is saved and I see its ID. Given the threshold is not a number, Then the form shows an error. Story B: As an SRE, I want to disable a rule temporarily, so that planned maintenance doesn't page anyone. Criteria: Given a rule is enabled, When I disable it, Then it stops firing. Then disabled rules are shown greyed out. Story C: As an on-call lead, I want rule changes audited, so that I can see who muted what. Criteria: When a rule is created, changed or disabled, Then an audit entry is recorded. Write the requirements document in the default Kiro spec location for this feature. Don't ask questions.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill fixes the default path (.kiro/specs/<kebab-case>/requirements.md), the document structure, and a BDD-to-EARS mapping (Given+When+Then -> Complex, error Given+Then -> Unwanted, Then-only -> Ubiquitous), and asks that responses become more specific and edge cases be added. Without it, models produce generic 'shall' statements or keep Given/When/Then.

floor_checks.text: Written at the default kebab-case path
Every numbered acceptance criterion contains SHALL
floor_checks.check: python3 -c "import re,sys;t=open('.kiro/specs/alert-rule-management/requirements.md').read();c=re.findall(r'(?m)^\s*\d+\.\s+(.*)$',t.split('## Requirements',1)[-1]);sys.exit(0 if c and all('SHALL' in x for x in c) else 1)"

rubric.criterion: BDD criteria map to the right EARS patterns
rubric.pass: Authenticated+submit -> 'WHILE ..., WHEN ..., THE ... SHALL'; non-numeric threshold -> 'IF ..., THEN THE ... SHALL'; enabled+disable -> Complex; 'disabled rules greyed out' -> Ubiquitous; audit -> Event-driven
rubric.partial: Most mapped correctly, one or two wrong patterns

rubric.criterion: Responses are more specific than the source
rubric.pass: Concrete values added (rule ID returned, validation message or HTTP 400, rule stops firing within a stated time, audit fields who/what/when)
Two or more relevant ones, e.g. unauthorized user, disabling an already-disabled rule, duration out of range, audit write failure

rubric.criterion: Criteria describe observable behavior, not implementation, and stay within the stories
rubric.pass: No database/table/framework details, no new features beyond the three stories
rubric.partial: One implementation detail or scope addition

rubric.pass: '# Requirements Document', '## Introduction', '## Requirements', one '### Requirement N' per story with **User Story:** and '#### Acceptance Criteria', 3-8 numbered criteria each
rubric.partial: Structure mostly right with one deviation (e.g. a requirement with 2 criteria)

focus: Could design start from this without re-asking product?

prompts.prompt: docs/stories/csv-export.md has the approved stories for our CSV export feature, but the acceptance criteria are vague ('quickly', 'many rows', 'it is blocked'). Turn them into the Kiro spec requirements document in the default spec location, with testable criteria. Don't ask questions; make reasonable concrete assumptions and note them in the Introduction.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's validation step bans vague terms without measurable values and requires Unwanted (IF/THEN) coverage of failures; its conversion rules decide each pattern. Generic output keeps soft wording or invents numbers without saying they are assumptions.
